Producer of Sterile and Non- Sterile Drug Products Specifically, Your firm failed to properly investigate the following failures: 1. Your fnm initiated a sterility test on 9/22/2017 for Isoproterenol HCL 4mcg/rrtl Injection, Lot #56771:14 with a BUD of 12/2112017. On 9/26/2017, Day 4 of the sterility test, growth was observed on the agar plates. Your fnm's sterility test has not been validated. A recall was conducted however, the recall effectiveness could not be determined since the provided records did not state what was returned, how many was returned and who was responsible to ensure that the items returned was received. Furthermore, the investigation involved sending one vial growth to be tested by [redacted] which came back sterile. The growth found on the plate was not sent for microbial identification. 2. On 2/13/2017, your firm conducted a bacterial endotoxin test on Ropivacaine 2mg/rrtl, Lot #53550:42. The test suitability failed and spike recovery failed. No investigation was conducted on this endotoxin test failure. This product was not recalled and distributed to your customer. 3. On 3/10/2017, your fnm received a consumer complaint regarding Glycopyrrolate 0.2mg/rrtl, Lot #53766:14 not working. The firm's investigation consisted of reviewing the formula worksheet of the batch, review of the COA of the active pharmaceutical ingredient and sent a sample to [redacted] for testing which confnmed the consumer's complaint. The potency of the product was tested at 32.9%. No root cause of the failure was determined and no recall was initiated. 4. Mitomycin Intl syringe 0.4mg/rrtl, Lot# 55337:00 was sent out for beyond use testing to Eagle Analytical Services. The initial test failed potency at 81.5%. No investigation was conducted for this failure and the product was distributed to your customer. Furthermore, a recall was not conducted.
